appearance_facts.fact: The California (CA) region is filled with the darkest maroon color visible on the map, appearing darker than the red fills of neighboring states like Nevada and Arizona.
The Texas (TX) region is filled with a very pale yellow color, appearing lighter than the orange fills of neighboring states like New Mexico and Oklahoma.
The Delaware (DE) region is filled with a medium orange color, appearing lighter than the dark red fills of neighboring states like Pennsylvania and Maryland.
The Minnesota (MN) region is filled with a dark red color, appearing darker than the orange fill of the neighboring Iowa region.
The Tennessee (TN) region is filled with a pale yellow color, appearing lighter than the dark red fills of neighboring states like Kentucky and Alabama.
The vertical color scale on the right side of the map transitions from pale yellow at the bottom to dark maroon at the top.

printed_facts.fact: The main title reads 'Incidence of Condition A in US States'.
The legend is labeled 'High' at the top (value 100) and 'Low' at the bottom, with intermediate values of 80, 60, 40, and 20.
A caption reads 'Clean choropleth: same US map base; darker color means higher true value.'
State abbreviations are printed in black text within their respective geographic boundaries.

public_definitions: Routing criterion: Highest incidence state in the dashboard
uncertain: The specific numeric incidence value for each state is not printed on the map, so the ranking is inferred solely from the relative darkness of the choropleth fills.
